description.p: Licoman is a native Linux desktop application (Rust + GPUI — no Electron, no embedded web view) that surfaces settings from shared/system capabilities, desktop environments, distributions and installed applications through one registry-driven interface.

Support is deliberately incremental and honestly labelled: rows show where their value came from (live service state, your configuration, declared defaults), and settings the running system cannot serve show truthful unavailable states instead of invented values. Writes go through a safe write engine with conflict checks, backups and readback verification; every write requires an explicit user action. Licoman runs unprivileged, has no sign-in, no telemetry and no background daemon.

ul.li: GNOME/GSettings — reads and gated writes through the native gio API
Xfce/Xfconf — live reads with per-row channel and property validation (read-only)
mpv — version-gated configuration reads and writes
Alacritty — TOML configuration with import merge and version validation
Hyprland — read-only compositor diagnostics over the documented IPC
power-profiles-daemon — typed property reads and writes

description.p: Unsupported applications stay visible in the Applications window with a real integration-status explanation. See the project's compatibility document for the tested matrix.

First public release candidate: registry-driven settings UI, environment discovery, read backends (GSettings, config files, D-Bus services, Xfconf, compositor IPC) and the safe write engine (files, GSettings, PowerProfiles). Alpha: expect rough edges and limited coverage; see the compatibility document.
